note_en: 比不上 and 比不过 mean "can't compare with, can't match": 这样的工具永远比不上真正理解学生情况的老师 "tools like this will never match a teacher who truly understands the student." Where English uses a separate verb ("match," "beat"), Chinese builds it from 比 "compare" plus a potential complement, with 不 in the middle for "cannot." The positive form, 比得上, means "is as good as."
